case.background: A fixed amount of air is trapped above mercury in a sealed J-tube. Add mercury pressure while holding the thermal condition fixed, then infer how pressure and air volume are related.
initial_observations: Adding mercury compresses the trapped air reversibly.
The bath prevents deliberate temperature changes during a run.

notes: The trapped amount of air and its temperature remain fixed.
Any non-empty subset of the two listed readouts may be requested.

experiment.intent: Probe a near-maximal compression to distinguish inverse (Boyle), sub-inverse (polytropic/adiabatic), and linear volume-pressure trends using both readouts.

hypotheses.statement: At fixed temperature and amount, absolute pressure times air volume is constant (Boyle): air_volume_ml = K / absolute_pressure_kpa, with absolute_pressure_kpa = ambient + added_pressure_kpa.
Compression is effectively adiabatic despite the bath: P V^gamma is constant with gamma=1.4, so air_volume_ml = C / (absolute_pressure_kpa^(1/1.4)).
Volume decreases approximately linearly with gauge pressure over the tested range: air_volume_ml = V0 - s*added_pressure_kpa.
A polytropic relation P V^n = const holds with n≈1.3 (between isothermal and adiabatic): air_volume_ml = C / (absolute_pressure_kpa^(1/1.3)).

experiment.intent: Probe the midpoint of the compression range (added 110 kPa, absolute 211.3 kPa) where Boyle (23.0 mL), polytropic/adiabatic (27-28 mL), and linear (31.5 mL) predictions are maximally separated, to identify the correct curvature.

hypotheses.statement: At fixed temperature and amount, absolute pressure times air volume is constant (Boyle): air_volume_ml = K / absolute_pressure_kpa, with absolute_pressure_kpa = ambient (101.3 kPa) + added_pressure_kpa. The 220 kPa point gives K = 321.3*15.1 = 4851.6 kPa*mL, implying V0 = 47.9 mL at ambient.
Volume decreases approximately linearly with gauge pressure: air_volume_ml = 47.9 - 0.149*added_pressure_kpa, fit through the observed 15.1 mL at 220 kPa.
A polytropic relation P V^n = const holds with n≈1.3: air_volume_ml = 47.9*(101.3/absolute_pressure_kpa)^(1/1.3), anchored at V0=47.9 mL.
Compression is effectively adiabatic: P V^1.4 constant, air_volume_ml = 47.9*(101.3/absolute_pressure_kpa)^(1/1.4), anchored at V0=47.9 mL.

hypotheses.statement: At fixed temperature and amount, absolute pressure times air volume is constant (Boyle): air_volume_ml = 4851.6 / absolute_pressure_kpa, with absolute_pressure_kpa = 101.3 + added_pressure_kpa. Confirmed exactly at both 220 kPa (15.1 mL) and 110 kPa (23.0 mL) added pressure.
A polytropic relation P V^n = const holds with n very close to 1 (0.95 < n < 1.05), observationally indistinguishable from Boyle's law over the tested range but differing outside it.
